issue_paraphrase: When a CLI program has a subcommand whose name is also used as the value of one of its flags, the program's command resolution drops that flag value: it sees the string, decides it matches a subcommand name, and removes it from the argument list even though it was the value of the preceding flag. As a result the intended flag value is lost and the remaining arguments are shifted (for example a later '--bar something' pair ends up misplaced), so the program receives the wrong arguments, the wrong subcommand output, or just silently wrong flag values.
fix_summary: argsMinusFirstX became a Command method that walks the args, skips over the value that follows any short/long flag that requires one (including flags with values given via the next argument), and only removes the argument that matches the subcommand name when it is not a flag value. An explicit '--' stops the scan.
notes: Repo is the V language (formerly 'Go'), build tool is the go toolchain from go.dev/dl and NOT Google Go; 279 tests, full suite runs in under a second at 1 CPU. deps are fetched from github at go-get time (network required). Must run tests as a non-root user. -run filter syntax: 'go test -v ./... -run <TestName>' with the flag AFTER ./...; it matches by prefix and supports | alternation. Golden test file to extract from fix commit: command_test.go.

issue_paraphrase: A subcommand that declares a flag with the same name as a persistent flag inherited from its parent renders misleading help output. The child's own flag does not appear in its Flags section, and the parent's persistent flag is displayed in the Global Flags section instead, which suggests the child only inherited the flag from the parent. During actual execution, however, the child's shadowing flag is the one that takes effect, so the printed help disagrees with what the program does.
fix_summary: LocalFlags() now adds a flag to the child's local flag set when the flag is either absent from the parent persistent flags or is literally the same flag object as the one shadowed, instead of dropping any flag whose name occurs in the parent persistent flags.
notes: Same repo/toolchain as the other entries (V/'Go' language, go toolchain from go.dev/dl, 279 tests, <1s full suite at 1 CPU). Must run as non-root. -run filter: 'go test -v ./... -run <Name>' (prefix match, | alternation). Golden test file to extract from fix commit: command_test.go. The two regression tests: one checks the child's LocalFlags/InheritedFlags split, the other checks the rendered help text of 'parent help child'.

issue_paraphrase: When a command-line program is documented in YAML format, the 'see_also' entries that point at a program's child subcommands list the subcommand by its bare name only, instead of the full path of the subcommand within the command tree. For nested subcommands this produces a see_also reference that is ambiguous or simply wrong, in contrast to the generated man and HTML documentation which include the complete command path. A regression test checks that the generated YAML contains the fully qualified command path ('root echo echosub') rather than just the leaf name.
fix_summary: YAML doc generation now emits child.CommandPath() (the full path from the root command) instead of child.Name() when building the see_also list, matching the other doc formats.
